geo.label: March lift-off; hike-size debate
parts: Macro Stance

The US reopens after Presidents' Day with a stale tape and a new shock. The S&P 500 closed 18 February at 4,348.87 index points, -0.72% on the day and -1.58% over five sessions, the Nasdaq 100 fell -1.14% to 14,009.54 index points and the VIX ended at 27.75 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Those prints predate Monday, when Reuters reported Vladimir Putin saying Russia must recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions [[n0218]] and the Atlantic Council analysed Moscow's order of troops into Ukraine [[n1137]]. Joe Biden had already said he was convinced Putin had decided to invade, the BBC reported [[n1267]]. The stance is Bearish: cash equities have not yet traded the recognition, and a Fed still debating the size of its first hike offers no policy cushion.
Rates & Curve

Treasury pricing is the binding constraint. The 2Y closed at 1.47% and the 10Y at 1.92%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +45 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18). Over 20 observations the 2Y rose +46 bps from 1.01% against +17 bps for the 10Y, a -29 bps compression: bear flattening on a curve that remains positively sloped. Over the last five observations the 2Y is -3 bps and the 10Y +0 bps, the first sign that haven demand is offsetting hike repricing. Reuters described a curve pricing Fed tightening and showing fears of policy error [[n1908]], and its poll still has 25 bps in March while calls for 50 bps grow louder [[n1139]]. A Fed governor opened the door to a half-point March hike, KALB reported [[n1933]], while the New York Fed president saw no need for a big one, per China Daily [[n1930]]. The DXY at 96.04 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) shows a firm but orderly dollar.
New / Most Important

The decisive change is that the Ukraine risk moved from troop counts to legal facts. Russian lawmakers' request for recognition had given Putin another card to play, CBS News said [[n1214]]. Washington's diplomacy was explicitly conditional: CNN reported the White House said Biden agreed to meet Putin in principle as long as Russia does not invade [[n1283]]. At home, Reuters said existing home sales accelerated as investors elbowed out first-time buyers [[n1879]], and mortgage rates of 3.92% are the highest in 33 months, the Orange County Register noted [[n1867]]. With US inflation at a 40-year high, as Global Data put it [[n1909]], a growth scare does not automatically buy a dovish pivot.
Playbook ✓

Action: run US equity exposure below benchmark into the first post-holiday session, funding overweights in energy (XLE) and staples (XLP) from long-duration growth (QQQ, ARKK). Trigger: an S&P 500 close below 4,348.87 index points with the VIX holding above 27.75 index points confirms the recognition shock is being priced rather than faded. What changes the call: sanctions that spare energy flows plus clear Fed pushback against a half-point opener would let the 2Y retrace part of its +46 bps rise and reopen the case for quality technology.

geo.label: ECB gradualism meets energy risk
parts: Macro Stance

Europe took the first hit. On 21 February the Euro Stoxx 50 fell -2.17% to 3,985.71 index points, the DAX -2.07% to 14,731.12 index points and the CAC 40 -2.04% to 6,788.34 index points, while the FTSE 100 lost only -0.39%, cushioned by Shell (-0.65%) and HSBC (+0.44%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Reuters had warned that European stocks were at risk if Russia invaded Ukraine [[n0708]]. The stance is Bearish because the region's exposure runs through gas, autos and banks, and its policy backstop is slow.
Activity & Inflation

Activity was improving before the shock: the Times of Malta reported eurozone growth jumping as virus restrictions eased [[n1135]], and DW said Germany plans an end to COVID restrictions [[n1100]]. Inflation is the constraint, with Reuters reporting UK inflation at 5.5%, the highest since 1992 [[n1111]]. Energy is the swing factor: Dutch TTF gas closed at 73.76 EUR/MWh, -6.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), but Reuters warned that while storage survived winter, summer refilling looms [[n1128]].
New / Most Important

The ECB is moving slowly: Reuters said Lagarde repeated her pledge for a gradual policy shift [[n1077]], and a Reuters poll has the deposit rate at -0.25% by year-end [[n1076]]. That leaves no quick buffer if gas supply is disrupted, and Reuters had already set out Europe's options in case of Russian gas disruption [[n1093]]. Banks are the transmission: Societe Generale fell -1.92% to 31.75 EUR and is -6.05% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21).
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Euro Stoxx 50 cyclicals and European autos against the FTSE 100's energy-and-bank mix. Trigger: a DAX close below 14,731.12 index points as sanctions details emerge. What changes the call: a negotiated pause that keeps TTF falling from 73.76 EUR/MWh, or a firmer ECB signal that removes the stagflation tail.

geo.label: PBOC easing; platform-fee crackdown
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy easing into the shock, but policy is pulling in two directions. The central bank cut key lending rates in January, including one for the first time in nearly two years, CNBC reported [[n0131]], and Bloomberg framed it as the PBOC seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0136]]. Yet regulators also ordered cuts to food-delivery fees, sparking a tech selloff, according to the WSJ [[n0693]]. The Shanghai Composite was flat (-0.00%) at 3,490.61 index points on 21 February but +1.80% over five sessions, while the Hang Seng fell -0.65% to 24,170.07 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Mixed: onshore support versus offshore regulatory risk.
PMIs & Activity

Activity entered February soft but stabilising. Reuters reported January factory activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit, per the Caixin PMI [[n0141]], while China Daily said industrial profits rebounded in 2021 as production improved [[n0139]]. Demand-side price pressure is cooling: Reuters said inflation slowed, leaving room for policy easing [[n0153]]. Reuters columnist Andy Home noted that metals imports boomed in 2021 and so did exports [[n0144]], a reminder that external demand carried the cycle. Pricing power survives at the premium end, with Starbucks and Tim Hortons raising prices in China, Reuters said [[n0564]], but Schindler warned on profit and China after a fourth-quarter earnings fall [[n0969]]. Hong Kong adds a drag: the BBC reported its hospitals overwhelmed amid a spike in cases [[n0170]]. The next official PMI print is the test of whether easing is reaching factories.
Credit Impulse

The credit signal is turning more supportive, but transmission is the open question. Al Jazeera reported the PBOC chief vowing support amid 'weak links' [[n0167]], and Fibre2Fashion detailed cuts to medium-term loan and reverse-repo rates [[n0134]], which lower bank funding costs. Cheaper money only becomes an impulse if developers, local governments and households want to borrow, and that demand has been the missing link. BNP Paribas Asset Management highlighted the US-China monetary policy divergence [[n1167]]: the more the Fed tightens while Beijing eases, the more the yuan, which Reuters said slipped under that divergence [[n0159]], becomes the pressure valve and limits how far rates can fall. The read is an impulse improving at the margin, not yet a broad credit upswing.
Property

Property is the weak link the PBOC chief alluded to, and Beijing's chosen channel is targeted. Khmer Times reported that China excluded affordable rental housing from property credit controls [[n0165]], a carve-out that supports social-housing construction without validating speculative demand. The January rate cuts [[n0131]] help mortgage borrowers at the margin, but a sales recovery requires confidence that pre-sold homes will be delivered, which rate cuts alone do not provide. Steel and iron ore demand therefore stays policy-managed: Reuters reported China urging some iron ore traders to reduce inventory [[n0045]], a sign that officials want to prevent restocking from running ahead of construction. The signal to watch is a broadening of credit exemptions beyond rental housing; until then property is a drag, not a driver.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade friction is rising on several fronts. The US added e-commerce sites run by Tencent and Alibaba to its 'notorious markets' list, Reuters reported [[n0200]], and the BBC said Washington accused China of 'serious harm' to workers through trade [[n1854]]; the Peterson Institute found China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports promised in the Trump-era deal [[n0147]]. The EU imposed anti-dumping tariffs on Chinese steel fasteners [[n0185]]. Geopolitics cuts both ways: Beijing sanctioned Lockheed and Raytheon again over Taiwan arms sales [[n0794]], and China said Western sanctions on Russia would worsen the Ukraine crisis, per the South China Morning Post [[n1193]]. Domestically, the fee order is regulation as redistribution, from platforms to merchants, and Bloomberg said it wiped $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0694]].
Markets & Flows

Offshore platforms bore the brunt. Tencent fell -5.23% to 423.03 HKD and Alibaba -3.85% to 114.90 HKD on 21 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21), after the Alibaba ADR lost -4.37% and KWEB -5.04% on 18 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The onshore tape was steadier, with ASHR +0.77% to 36.82 USD on 18 February and +2.22% over five sessions. Sell-side calls had turned constructive: CNBC reported banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0155]], and Business Insider noted Tencent joining the world's ten most valuable companies as Meta slid [[n0561]]. Index changes keep hardware in focus, with Lenovo selected as a Hang Seng Index constituent [[n0762]].
New / Most Important

The new information is regulatory rather than macro: the food-delivery fee order [[n0693]] revived the template of policy-driven margin transfers just as foreign banks turned positive. Russia's move on the Donbas adds a second layer. The Atlantic Council described Russia and China as partners in dedollarization [[n0198]], so if Western measures extend to dollar clearing, secondary-sanction risk for Chinese banks and commodity traders becomes a tail to price. Hong Kong's outbreak is now a political priority, with Xi urging the city to control surging cases, New Hampshire Public Radio reported [[n0182]], which raises the odds of tighter restrictions on mainland-Hong Kong traffic.
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR, Shanghai Composite) over offshore platforms (KWEB, Tencent) while the fee order is digested. Trigger: add offshore only if Tencent stabilises above 423.03 HKD while the Shanghai Composite holds its +1.80% five-session gain. What changes the call: a broad property-credit loosening would make the trade more pro-cyclical, while a second platform pricing order or Russia-linked secondary sanctions would hit both legs. ⚠ Divergence: banks call Chinese stocks a buy [[n0155]] and the onshore index is rising, yet Tencent fell -5.23% and KWEB -5.04% in consecutive sessions; easing and regulatory tightening are being priced at the same time.

geo.label: BOJ dovish; board reshuffle watch
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is a relative shelter rather than a winner. The Nikkei 225 fell -0.78% to 26,910.87 index points on 21 February and is -2.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Reuters reported that the economy rebounded in the fourth quarter on solid spending, with Omicron clouding the outlook [[n1315]], and CNBC said February factory activity growth fell to a five-month low [[n1338]]. Mixed: policy stays easy, but as an energy importer Japan is exposed to the oil leg of the crisis through its trade balance.
Activity & Currency

The external account is the pressure point. Al Jazeera reported exports growing less than expected as the trade deficit soared [[n1331]], and the Seattle Times had reported imports hitting record highs on surging energy prices [[n1300]]. With Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), every leg higher in crude widens that deficit, which dilutes the yen's usual haven appeal. Policy remains the anchor: Reuters said a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1322]], but board turnover is a gradual channel. Equities transmit the chip cycle: Tokyo Electron fell -2.94% to 55,140.00 JPY and Advantest -1.88% to 9,380.00 JPY, while Sony is -8.22% over 20 sessions at 11,890.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). TSMC's plan to expand its new Japan chip factory, with Denso taking a stake, per the Asahi Shimbun [[n1325]], is a medium-term support.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold Japan at neutral, preferring exporters with pricing power over energy-intensive domestics, and size semicap positions (Tokyo Electron, Advantest) for volatility. Trigger: a Nikkei 225 close below 26,910.87 index points with Brent above 93.54 USD/bbl would show the trade-deficit channel dominating. What changes the call: a firmer BOJ signal from the reshuffle, or crude retreating on an Iran deal, which would ease the import bill.

geo.label: RBA patient; won't follow the Fed
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is the commodity hedge inside a risk-off Asia. The S&P/ASX 200 rose +0.16% to 7,233.60 index points on 21 February, with BHP +0.58% to 42.95 AUD and Rio Tinto +0.80% to 120.20 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21), while ABC reported AGL rejecting the Atlassian billionaire's takeover bid [[n0066]]. The RBA is the brake on rate risk: the WSJ reported the central bank won't follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0053]]. Mixed.
Demand & Financing

Labour and prices argue the RBA is behind the curve. The Australian reported the jobless rate at a 13-year low as a hike loomed [[n0002]], and the AFR's 'shock' CPI headline put inflation at 3.5 per cent [[n0007]]. Inflation expectations rose to 4.9% in January, per Roy Morgan [[n0060]]. Results show the margin squeeze: Reuters said Coles flagged inflation as cost controls limited its H1 profit dip [[n0068]], and Wesfarmers' profit dipped after a 'perfect pandemic storm' [[n0470]]. Australian Broker News reported CBA's prediction of when rates will rise [[n0058]], a reminder that bank margins hinge on the RBA's timing.
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight the big miners (BHP, Rio Tinto) as a supply-disruption hedge and stay neutral on banks, with CBA at 98.09 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Trigger: an RBA shift toward hiking would favour banks. What changes the call: Beijing's iron ore inventory guidance [[n0045]] is the risk to miners, and Fortescue's -13.80% five-session slide to 19.61 AUD shows how fast iron ore sentiment can turn.

geo.label: NBP hiking into frontline risk
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is the EU market closest to the escalation, and the tape shows it. Bankier.pl reported the WIG20 at its lowest since May 2021, with fear on the equity market, on 21 February [[n1537]]. The macro mix leaves little cushion: Forsal reported January inflation of 9.2% from the statistics office GUS [[n1419]], and Rzeczpospolita said the Monetary Policy Council's latest hike took rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1399]]. Imported energy inflation, rising rates and a security shock on the eastern border form a stagflationary set-up for domestic cyclicals and a risk-premium shock for banks. Money.pl reported that Fitch, in its rating decision, pointed to high inflation and problems with the European Commission [[n1514]]. Stance: Bearish.
Markets

The 21 February session was a bank-led liquidation. The Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker fell -2.70% to 36.00 PLN and is -3.77% over 20 sessions, while Bank Pekao dropped -6.75% to 119.50 PLN, mBank -6.00% to 426.20 PLN, PKO Bank Polski -4.17% to 43.86 PLN and PZU -3.77% to 33.21 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). In dollar terms the selling began earlier: EPOL lost -1.65% to 20.24 USD on 18 February and is -4.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The irony is that banks are the clearest beneficiaries of NBP hikes; the market is overriding net-interest-income upside with a country-risk premium. Deposit pricing is lagging policy, which supports margins: Analizy.pl noted the average deposit rate rose clearly in December [[n1497]], yet Obserwator Gospodarczy asked why bank deposit rates are not rising [[n1416]]. The zloty is the transmission to watch, because a weaker currency would add to imported inflation and force the NBP's hand.
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal politics are noisy. Biznes Wprost reported dismissals at the finance ministry over the Polski Ład tax reform [[n1529]], and Next Gazeta said President Duda, having signed Polski Ład, now wants comprehensive changes, a possible Polski Ład 2.0 [[n1442]]. Money.pl argued that public debt will rise because of the NBP and grow more costly over time [[n1512]], and Business Insider Polska carried an expert explaining how rate hikes raise the cost of public debt [[n1519]]. On EU money, Reuters reported the top EU court threw out the Polish and Hungarian challenge to the rule-of-law conditionality mechanism [[n1365]]; Rzeczpospolita said Justice Minister Ziobro then attacked Prime Minister Morawiecki [[n1464]], while EUobserver reported Poland edging toward a rule-of-law deal [[n1374]]. Unlocking EU recovery funds is the largest domestic upside catalyst; the coalition's internal fight is the obstacle.
Corporate & Sectors

Commodity names are the internal hedge. JSW, the coking-coal miner, is +21.66% over 20 sessions at 41.85 PLN despite a -6.00% drop on 21 February, and KGHM is +12.88% at 152.45 PLN after only -0.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Governance risk is live at JSW: Wyborcza reported the anti-corruption bureau CBA found irregularities at JSW Koks over a 289 mln zł investment [[n1526]]. KGHM is positioning for nuclear, with eKoszalin reporting small modular reactors in Poland as early as 2029 [[n1426]]. Consumer and tech names are weaker: StockWatch.pl said Allegro shares hit new lows [[n1505]], and the stock is -14.99% over 20 sessions at 31.20 PLN even as Wiadomości Handlowe reported more than five million Allegro Smart users [[n1538]]. CD Projekt fell -3.32% to 169.00 PLN as Antyweb reported the Witcher 3 director leaving to found Rebel Wolves [[n1461]], overshadowing the next-generation Cyberpunk 2077 release [[n1407]]. Utilities slid, PGE -4.66% to 7.20 PLN and Tauron -5.32% to 2.26 PLN, as Newsweek asked whether PGE was hiding a report on the Turów disaster [[n1456]]. Dino is -15.99% over 20 sessions at 289.00 PLN, with DlaHandlu.pl reporting Aldi, Biedronka, Dino and Lidl hiring almost 2,300 people [[n1459]], a wage-cost signal for discounters.
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is becoming NATO's frontline logistics hub. Reuters reported the US announced Abrams tanks for Poland as the Russia threat mounts [[n1375]], The National Interest said additional US F-15s were sent to bolster NATO's eastern flank [[n1367]], and the American Homefront Project reported Fort Bragg's 82nd Airborne deploying to Poland [[n1343]]. Warsaw signed a trilateral agreement with the UK and Ukraine 'in face of Russian aggression', per Notes From Poland [[n1371]], and on 21 February Gazeta Prawna reported the prime minister raising the alert level for cyberspace threats [[n1534]]. Belarus is the second front: the Guardian reported Russian troops will remain there indefinitely [[n1280]], and wnp.pl said work on the border barrier with Belarus is running on three shifts [[n1484]]. Energy security is the economic channel: WysokieNapiecie.pl asked what will flow through Baltic Pipe and Yamal a year from now [[n1528]], InformNapalm described the Lithuania-Poland GIPL interconnector as part of new gas geopolitics [[n1378]], and Money.pl reported firms switching en masse to consumer gas tariffs [[n1520]].
New / Most Important

The decisive new fact is Moscow's move on the Donbas: Reuters reported Putin saying Russia must recognise the breakaway regions [[n0218]], and the Kremlin published the president's address [[n1284]]. For Poland that turns a diplomatic crisis into a potential refugee, sanctions and energy-flow shock. Diplomacy had already hit a wall: TVN24 quoted Foreign Minister Rau, after talks with Lavrov, saying European security is in deep crisis [[n1435]], and Interia reported Russia's Maria Zakharova claiming the Polish government acts in US rather than national interests [[n1478]]. Opposition leader Donald Tusk said the situation in Ukraine will decide whether Poland is safe, PolsatNews reported [[n1490]]. Notes From Poland reported the US opening a welcome centre in Poland for citizens fleeing Ukraine [[n1366]], an early sign of the logistics load to come.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish banks and the WIG20 tracker, hedging residual exposure with JSW and KGHM rather than chasing utilities. Trigger: a close below 36.00 PLN in the WIG20TR tracker, or bank losses extending beyond Pekao's -6.75% day, would signal a sanctions-and-refugee premium being built in. What changes the call: a credible de-escalation, since Biden's summit offer was conditional on no invasion, CNBC reported [[n1270]], or an EU recovery-fund deal that pairs margin upside with lower country risk. ⚠ Divergence: the Monetary Policy Council's hikes [[n1399]] should be lifting bank earnings, yet Pekao and mBank fell -6.75% and -6.00% in a day while JSW keeps a +21.66% 20-session gain; investors are paying for commodity scarcity and selling the rate beneficiaries.
Narrative

Tech enters the reopen caught between rates and geopolitics. XLK closed 18 February at 152.44 USD, -1.01% on the day and -1.22% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft -0.96% to 287.93 USD and Apple -0.94% to 167.30 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). For software multiples, the bear-flattening curve matters more than the Donbas.
Reported

Cisco defied the doubters with a beat and raise, CNBC said [[n0959]], adding $15 billion of buybacks, per Reuters [[n0947]]; the stock is +6.14% over five sessions at 57.21 USD. Software was sold: Adobe is -6.63% and Salesforce -5.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
EPS Upside Watch

Networking and hardware with pricing power, such as Cisco and Arista at 125.92 USD (+4.13% over five sessions), can beat if supply chains ease, while seat-based software faces normalising growth after the pandemic pull-forward.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Fortune asked how low tech stocks can fall [[n0803]], and Business Insider relayed elite investors' warning that the market hit 'peak stupid' [[n0788]]. Those warnings target unprofitable growth, not cash-rich incumbents: buybacks at Cisco's scale turn old tech into a defensive asset.
Narrative

Communication services is the weakest large sector. XLC closed at 67.41 USD, -6.66% over 20 sessions, dragged by Meta Platforms (FB) at 206.16 USD, -32.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Bloomberg said Meta lost its top-10 ranking by market value amid its worst month ever [[n0619]].
Reported

Roku revenue missed on supply-chain snags and shares fell 20%, Reuters reported [[n0639]], and Paramount shares slumped as investment to beef up streaming spooked investors [[n0466]]. Spotify is -22.12% over 20 sessions at 152.27 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) as Forbes reported Joe Rogan's deal at a reported $200 million [[n1705]].
EPS Upside Watch

Alphabet (2,608.06 USD, +0.04% over 20 sessions) and Netflix (+1.19% to 391.29 USD on 18 February) are holding up. The WSJ's account of Facebook's $10 billion breakup with advertisers [[n1016]] shows ad budgets being reallocated, which favours search and commerce data over social feeds.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Snap is +18.34% over 20 sessions at 38.01 USD despite sharing Meta's ad exposure. That dispersion says the trade is stock-specific: short business models exposed to ad-measurement loss and long-duration content spending, not the whole sector.
Narrative

Financials sit at the centre of the rate-versus-risk tension. XLF closed flat (-0.03%) at 39.22 USD and is +2.67% over 20 sessions, with KRE +2.70% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). A 2Y up +46 bps in 20 observations lifts asset yields, but the -29 bps compression in 10Y-2Y caps the term-spread benefit (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Goldman Sachs lifted its targets in a bid to win over skeptics, Reuters reported [[n0591]], while Bank of America's CEO said its capital-markets business is down but pipelines are full [[n0547]]. AIG's profit beat estimates on general insurance strength, per Reuters [[n0945]].
EPS Upside Watch
Net interest income is the upside lever: JPMorgan (152.14 USD, +4.87% over 20 sessions) and Wells Fargo (+3.65%) gain if March lift-off proceeds without a credit event.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Reuters reported Wall Street banks fearing inflation, asset-price deflation and even recession [[n0099]]: the banks themselves are flagging the flattening risk. Morgan Stanley's -8.75% five-session drop to 95.42 USD, as Reuters said its role in the Archegos collapse sped up block-trade probes [[n0457]], shows that capital-markets franchises carry legal tail risk deposit banks do not.
Narrative

Energy is the hedge that pays. Brent closed at 93.54 USD/bbl (+6.43% over 20 sessions) and WTI at 91.07 USD/bbl, while XLE is +8.97% over 20 sessions at 68.05 USD despite a -3.35% five-session pullback (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Bloomberg argued oil's spectacular Covid crash set the world up for $100 crude [[n0085]].
Reported

Norway's oil firms hiked their 2022 investment plans, Reuters said [[n0626]], and Tenaris saw a further boost to sales and margins in H1, per Offshore Engineer [[n1003]]. Glencore reported record earnings while setting aside $1.5 billion for probes, Reuters reported [[n0919]].
EPS Upside Watch

Supply is tight on policy: Middle East Eye reported Saudi Arabia rejecting a US request to raise output [[n1120]], and Bloomberg reported Marathon's huge Louisiana refinery rocked by an explosion and fire [[n0808]], supportive for refining margins. Exxon Mobil (77.36 USD) and Chevron (133.42 USD) carry the most direct leverage to Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The bearish risk is diplomatic, not geological: the WSJ reported the US nearing a return to the Iran nuclear deal [[n1291]], and Reuters said Asian refiners are eager to resume Iranian oil imports [[n1688]]. A deal would add barrels just as the Russia premium peaks.
Narrative

Industrials are splitting between defence and the cycle. XLI closed at 98.34 USD, -2.83% over 20 sessions; Caterpillar is -10.34% at 191.95 USD while General Dynamics is +4.49% at 215.82 USD over the same 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Deere aimed for bigger profit as price hikes powered an earnings beat, Reuters reported [[n0698]], yet the stock fell -3.00% to 369.10 USD on the day. Airbus soared back out of the red, per Statista [[n1686]], while the WSJ said its plan to ramp up production of its bestselling jet hit snags [[n0538]].
EPS Upside Watch

Defence primes have the cleanest upside: Raytheon Technologies (RTX) is +7.06% over 20 sessions at 93.37 USD and Lockheed Martin +4.11% at 386.46 USD, even after Beijing sanctioned both again over Taiwan arms sales [[n0794]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Freight is the hidden margin threat: FreightWaves quoted an economist calling freight-rate hikes over the past two years unprecedented [[n1718]], and Bloomberg warned the US freight-cost blowout may mean little inflation relief soon [[n1680]]. Pricing power, not volume, decides industrial EPS.
Narrative

Discretionary demand is cooling at the margin. XLY closed at 180.00 USD, -0.23% over 20 sessions, but beneath the index Amazon is +6.98% while Tesla is -9.21% at 856.98 USD and Carvana -10.58% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Airbnb beat on earnings and gave strong guidance, CNBC reported [[n0232]]; DoorDash revenue beat and shares soared 24%, per Reuters [[n0419]], before giving back -8.40% on 18 February. Kering shares surged as Gucci sales rebounded, Bloomberg said [[n0609]], while Reuters reported production caps curbing growth at Hermes [[n0730]].
EPS Upside Watch

Home improvement is the test: mortgage rates at their highest since May 2019, per Realtor.com [[n1865]], hit big-ticket housing spending first, and the Motley Fool's case that Home Depot is a better business than Lowe's [[n1014]] frames the quality split.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla's regulatory overhang is growing, with Reuters reporting a US investigation into 416,000 vehicles over unexpected braking [[n1711]], but the larger risk is fuel: Spectrum News explained how a Ukraine-Russia conflict could lift gas prices [[n1206]], a direct tax on lower-income spending.
Narrative

Staples are the earnings-certainty trade. XLP is +1.04% over five sessions at 76.03 USD and rose +0.18% on 18 February, with Coca-Cola +3.73% over five sessions at 62.54 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Walmart's profits grew as consumers continued to spend, the New York Times reported [[n0663]], and Modern Retail said it gained grocery share thanks to continued inflation [[n0661]]. Kraft Heinz beat on raised prices and robust demand, per ET Retail [[n0612]], and Reuters said Nestle is confident cost inflation won't bite margins [[n0621]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power drives the upside: Procter & Gamble (+2.31% over five sessions, 159.90 USD) and PepsiCo can pass through costs while volumes hold, and Walmart at 137.99 USD is the cleanest trade-down beneficiary.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The risk is a consumer crack: CNBC reported Walmart saying shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0664]], and Reuters said European retailers are taking on food giants in hard bargains [[n0588]]. Staples outperform until retailer pushback caps price increases.
Narrative

Health care is defensive but not uniform. XLV fell -2.10% over five sessions to 127.51 USD, with Moderna -9.66% and Pfizer -4.43% over five sessions, while AbbVie is +9.13% over 20 sessions at 144.03 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Moderna's CEO said it is reasonable to think the pandemic may be in its final stages, CNBC reported [[n0451]], and Reuters said the company eyes a COVID booster by August [[n0453]], a fading-revenue narrative for vaccine makers.
EPS Upside Watch

Pipelines drive dispersion: Bayer hiked Nubeqa's peak-sales goal to more than €3B, per Fierce Pharma [[n0987]], and Bristol Myers won FDA priority review for its CAR-T drug Breyanzi [[n0988]]. Eli Lilly (240.31 USD) and the Novo Nordisk ADR (+5.72% over 20 sessions) carry growth-quality exposure.
⚡ Breaking Convention

STAT noted that some newly public biotech companies trade below cash [[n1571]]; XBI at 89.39 USD (-4.24% over five sessions) is pricing financing risk that a hawkish Fed sharpens. The defensive label belongs to cash-generative pharma, not the biotech tail.
Narrative

Materials are becoming a supply-shock trade. Aluminum closed at 3,304.50 USD/t, +9.20% over 20 sessions, and palladium at 2,335.40 USD/oz, +11.19%, while XLB is flat at 83.86 USD (-0.21%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Reuters warned commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions [[n0696]].
Reported
DuPont agreed to shed its mobility and materials unit in an $11 bln Celanese deal, Reuters reported [[n0704]], a portfolio-pruning model Barron's used to call DuPont a buy [[n0702]].
EPS Upside Watch

Alcoa is +39.12% over 20 sessions at 78.20 USD and Mosaic +14.47% at 45.00 USD, and Macau Business reported nickel prices soaring on Russia tension and tight supply [[n1738]]. Producers outside Russia gain pricing power if flows are disrupted.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Chemicals sit on the wrong side of the same shock: European producers buy gas at TTF 73.76 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), so a supply scare squeezes their margins even as it rewards metals. Barrick's CEO suggesting miners are overpaying for assets amid higher gold prices, per the Financial Post [[n0548]], is a late-cycle warning.
Narrative

Real estate is the clearest rate casualty. XLRE closed at 44.68 USD, -4.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), as the 10Y rose +17 bps to 1.92% over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Private capital is still buying: Reuters said three large law firms crafted a $5.8 bln Blackstone real estate buy [[n0495]], the New York Times reported Blackstone expanding further into US rental housing [[n0406]], and Bloomberg said Wynn Resorts sold a Boston property to Realty Income for $1.7 billion [[n0386]].
EPS Upside Watch

Rents give landlords pricing power: the Joint Center for Housing Studies said rents soared across the country, though home prices grew even faster [[n0636]]. Residential and logistics REITs can grow cash flow; offices cannot. Reuters reported Blackstone and partners betting $24 billion on hunger for urgent delivery [[n0243]], a private-market mark for logistics.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The Washington Post reported investors bought a record share of homes in 2021 [[n1848]]. When listed REITs trade down while private buyers pay up, the discount becomes the catalyst, but only after the 2Y stops rising.
Narrative

Utilities are trading as bond proxies, not havens. XLU is -3.81% over 20 sessions at 66.22 USD, with NextEra -10.23% and Southern Company -5.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The driver is the 10Y's +17 bps rise to 1.92% over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18): allowed returns reset slowly while discount rates reprice immediately.
Reported

Reuters reported EDF getting $2 bln of state help over nuclear-plant outages [[n0706]], WABE said Georgia Power's $30B nuclear plant is delayed up to six more months [[n0519]], and POWER Magazine reported Duke Energy eyeing a coal phaseout by 2035 [[n0576]].
EPS Upside Watch
Southern Company's CEO said hybrid work is driving residential energy demand, CNBC reported [[n0600]], a volume tailwind; Duke at 99.81 USD (+1.09% on 18 February) is the quality defensive.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Forbes reported France vowing to build more nuclear energy after high natural-gas prices [[n1640]]. Europe's energy shock is a capex mandate, which favours grid and nuclear suppliers over rate-sensitive regulated utilities; in the US, the stronger defensive is the low-beta balance sheet, not the green-growth multiple.
Narrative

European autos are the sector most exposed to the escalation. The iShares SXAP tracker fell -2.53% to 59.72 EUR on 21 February, with BMW -3.24% to 92.29 EUR, Volkswagen preference shares -2.84% to 174.98 EUR, Renault -3.98% to 34.88 EUR and Mercedes-Benz Group -2.06% to 74.03 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21).
Reported

Volkswagen expects the chip shortage to ease later in 2022, Reuters reported [[n1681]], and Mercedes-Benz foresees EV-only production lines within a few years [[n0809]]. Reuters, citing Manager Magazin, said Volkswagen is in talks with Huawei on an autonomous-driving unit [[n0659]], which adds China-partnership exposure to the investment case.
EPS Upside Watch
Supply normalisation is the upside: easier chip supply means volume recovery in the second half, which is why Mercedes-Benz Group is still +8.39% and Renault +7.72% over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Energy, not chips, is now the binding constraint: Reuters warned of the summer gas refill [[n1128]], and parts plants are energy-intensive. Obserwator Gospodarczy reported German car production 40% below its level three years ago [[n1403]]; recovery starts from a deep hole, and an energy shock would delay it.
Narrative

Semis are holding up better than software. SOXX is +0.55% over five sessions at 466.57 USD and the PHLX Semiconductor Index closed at 3,384.30 index points, while ASML's US line is -6.75% over 20 sessions at 647.83 USD and the TSMC ADR -4.19% at 119.31 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Reported

Al Jazeera reported Nvidia forecasting upbeat current-quarter revenue [[n1661]], yet the stock fell -3.53% to 236.42 USD on 18 February. Intel announced its 18A node, per TechPowerUp [[n1720]], and fell -5.32% to 45.04 USD as SemiAnalysis asked whether its kitchen-sink turnaround is reasonable [[n1721]].
EPS Upside Watch

Capacity commitments signal demand: TechSpot reported Nvidia spent $10 billion for a chunk of TSMC's 5nm capacity [[n1739]], and TSMC is expanding its Japan factory [[n1325]]. AMD's market cap surpassed Intel's for the first time, per Tom's Hardware [[n0227]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The geopolitical risk is supply chains, not demand: South Korea's trade minister said the Russia-Ukraine crisis could disrupt supply chains, CNBC reported [[n1238]]. Samsung (74,300.00 KRW) and SK Hynix (131,500.00 KRW) were flat on 21 February while Tokyo Electron fell -2.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21), so Asia is pricing equipment risk more than memory.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power paid; pandemic normalisation punished
parts: Rewarded

Companies that showed pricing power or returned cash were rewarded. Cisco's $15 billion buyback alongside a raised forecast, per Reuters [[n0947]], lifted the stock +6.14% over five sessions to 57.21 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Airbnb's beat and strong guidance, reported by CNBC [[n0232]], left it +5.03% over five sessions. The AFR said Treasury Wine shares surged as it lifted some luxury brand prices [[n0178]], Bloomberg said Kering shares surged as Gucci sales rebounded [[n0609]], and Bloomberg argued Walmart has a cart full of reasons to love inflation [[n0660]].
Punished

Pandemic winners whose growth is normalising were sold hard. CNBC reported Roblox closing down 26% after an earnings miss [[n0477]] and Shopify closing down 16% after warning that the pandemic boost will fade [[n0484]]; Shopify is -23.08% over five sessions at 656.88 USD. Reuters said Palantir's margins will take a hit from higher spending in its commercial push [[n0631]], and the stock is -16.07% over five sessions at 11.02 USD. DraftKings fell -21.62% on 18 February to 17.29 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), a session that echoed Yahoo Finance's case that sports betting is a low-margin business [[n0978]].
Pattern

The market pays for current cash flow and punishes spending for future growth. Even beats are sold when the reaction function is driven by multiples: Deere's price-led beat [[n0698]] met a -3.00% session, and Nvidia's fourth-quarter results [[n0084]] were followed by a -1.28% five-session move as the 2Y sat at 1.47%. Guidance that implies margin compression is the common thread among the losers; buybacks and pricing are the common thread among the winners.
Attention into EPS

TipRanks flagged the most notable earnings for the week starting Feb 21, 2022 [[n0810]], and the attention is shifting from pandemic platforms to housing-linked retail and consumer staples. The Motley Fool's argument that Home Depot is a better business than Lowe's [[n1014]] sets up a quality comparison in home improvement, where guidance on 2022 sales matters more than the quarter.
Playbook

Own beat-and-return stories (Cisco, Walmart) and avoid names reporting against pandemic comparisons; fade post-earnings pops where guidance implies margin compression. Trigger: keep the bias while the VIX holds above 27.75 index points. What changes the call: a VIX retreat below that level would let the market reward strong guides with multiple expansion again.

underowned.title: Gold miners as the overlooked haven
parts: Attention Gap

Gold has quietly outperformed while attention sits on crypto and tech. Bullion closed at 1,899.80 USD/oz, +3.13% over five sessions, and GDX is +9.00% over 20 sessions at 34.50 USD, with Newmont +5.97% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Money.pl reported gold prices rising as Ukrainian companies lost ground on the conflict [[n1477]].
Exposure & Risk

Miners give operating leverage to bullion, but cost inflation erodes it, and Barrick's CEO warned that miners are overpaying for assets [[n0548]]. A hawkish Fed that lifts real yields is the main risk.
Trigger to Watch

Sanctions on Russian finance would favour bullion as a reserve asset, with the Atlantic Council's dedollarization framing [[n0198]] as the long-run bid. Gold falling back below its 21 January level of 1,831.80 USD/oz would end the trade.

underowned.title: Fertiliser and grains as the food-security trade
parts: Attention Gap

Food is the under-discussed Russia channel. Al Jazeera's infographic on Russia, Ukraine and the global wheat supply [[n1701]] and MarketWatch's warning that the crisis may make food-price inflation even worse [[n1649]] point to inputs. Soybeans are +13.24% over 20 sessions at 1,601.50 US cents/bu and corn +6.17% at 654.25 US cents/bu, while wheat is only +2.18% at 797.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
Exposure & Risk
Mosaic (+14.47% over 20 sessions) and Nutrien (+7.00%) carry the input exposure; CF Industries fell -3.83% on 18 February, a reminder that gas-based nitrogen margins move with fuel costs.
Trigger to Watch

Disruption to Black Sea shipping or sanctions on Russian fertiliser would tighten supply; a Reuters commentary noted Ukraine's unmatched corn crop gains encroaching on rival exporters [[n1690]], which shows how much grain capacity sits in the conflict zone.

underowned.title: US natural gas as Europe's swing supplier
parts: Attention Gap

Henry Hub gas closed at 4.43 USD/MMBtu, +12.43% over five sessions, while TTF sits at 73.76 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The EIA forecasts US marketed natural gas production rising in 2022 and 2023 [[n1712]], and Brookings argued now is not the time to limit US natural gas exports [[n1130]].
Exposure & Risk
ConocoPhillips (89.63 USD, +8.35% over 20 sessions) is a direct US gas producer exposure; the risk is that export capacity, not molecules, caps how much Europe can import in the near term.
Trigger to Watch

Any disruption of Russian pipeline flows: Reuters' map of Russian gas pipeline exports to Europe [[n0640]] shows the volumes at stake. Beijing Gas's talks over a ten-year Shell LNG deal [[n0549]] show Asian buyers competing for the same cargoes.

underowned.title: Uranium and the nuclear build-out
parts: Attention Gap

Nuclear policy momentum is building while the stocks fall. Cameco is -9.12% over five sessions at 20.22 USD and URA -4.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), even as POWER Magazine reported Poland securing a NuScale SMR as urgency for nuclear energy ramps up across Central and Eastern Europe [[n1347]].
Exposure & Risk

Centrus Energy (40.04 USD, -9.58% over five sessions) adds fuel-cycle exposure, with Cameco and URA the liquid proxies. Timelines are long and delays common: WABE reported Georgia Power's nuclear plant delayed up to six more months [[n0519]], and utility contracting can lag policy by years.
Trigger to Watch

France's pledge to build more nuclear energy [[n1640]] and further SMR orders are the policy triggers; a reversal of URA's -4.58% five-session slide would confirm that the market is starting to price them.

crypto.title: Bitcoin trades as risk, not refuge
parts: Market Context

Crypto absorbed the 21 February escalation in real time, and it did not behave like a haven. Bitcoin's daily close was 37,075.28 USD, -3.53% on the day, -15.66% from 16 February and -4.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-21). Ether fell -2.09% to 2,573.82 USD and is -17.71% over five days, Solana dropped -8.56% to 83.12 USD, XRP -9.61% to 0.70 USD and Dogecoin -6.12% to 0.13 USD, so the higher-beta tokens fell hardest. Equity proxies were already slipping on 18 February: GBTC fell -3.67% to 24.66 USD, Marathon Digital -7.12% to 23.89 USD, Coinbase Global -1.44% to 189.16 USD and Block (SQ) -6.06% to 97.72 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18).
New / Most Important

The narrative is turning defensive. Bloomberg reported Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin saying crypto 'welcomes' another winter [[n0875]], and the Financial Stability Board warned of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n0851]]. Yahoo Finance described how the 'Big Short DAO' bet against the crypto market and won [[n0861]]. Long-horizon capital is still arriving, with Forbes reporting Sequoia's $500 million fund for crypto tokens [[n0864]] and Ledger Insights saying stablecoin firm Circle doubled its valuation to $9 billion in a new SPAC deal [[n1159]], but venture money does not defend daily prices. Regulatory friction persists: CoinGeek said the FCA is concerned about Binance's backdoor re-entry into the UK payments network [[n0881]], and Reuters reported El Salvador's Bukele telling bitcoin-wary US senators to stay out of internal affairs [[n0849]], which keeps sovereign adoption politically contested.
Playbook

Action: stay underweight crypto and the miners while Bitcoin trades with the Nasdaq 100 rather than with gold. Trigger to add: a daily close back above the 38,743.27 USD of 1 February, with ether recovering its five-day loss. What changes the call: if sanctions on Russia push capital toward non-bank rails, Bitcoin could decouple, but the 21 February close points the other way. Risk: MicroStrategy at 395.97 USD and the miners amplify any further leg down.

flows.title: Liquidity tightens as the haven bid starts
parts: Global Liquidity

The liquidity regime is turning from abundant to rationed. Capital Economics argued 'we need to talk about QT' [[n1138]], and Reuters examined what could drive the Fed to a 'Plan B' for balance-sheet reduction [[n1160]]. Eurodollar futures are betting a hawkish Fed could ease rates, slightly, in 2024, Reuters reported [[n1127]], which means the market is pricing a short, sharp cycle. The offsets are partial: China's central bank is easing [[n0136]], the ECB moves gradually [[n1077]], and the Bank of Japan is still applying a negative rate to MUFG Bank deposits, the Asahi Shimbun reported [[n1306]], so yen and euro funding stay cheap even as dollar funding tightens. Bloomberg reported an obscure corner of Wall Street making billions trading inflation [[n1134]], a reminder that inflation protection, not duration, has been the profitable rates exposure. The Fed's January readout showed it is not wed to a particular pace of hikes, Reuters said [[n1916]], keeping the March decision as the global liquidity pivot.
Rates & Dollar

The curve is doing the Fed's work: the 2Y at 1.47% (+46 bps in 20 observations) and the 10Y at 1.92% (+17 bps) leave 10Y-2Y at +45 bps, still positively sloped but bear flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18). The haven bid is visible in duration ETFs: TLT rose +1.05% to 138.23 USD and IEF +0.32% to 111.22 USD on 18 February, though both remain down over 20 sessions at -3.76% and -1.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The DXY at 96.04 index points is +0.42% over 20 sessions, steady rather than spiking. Bloomberg warned that Treasury market liquidity is eroding with the Fed's course a gamble [[n1905]], which raises the risk of air pockets in a geopolitical rush for duration. The yuan slipping on policy divergence [[n0159]] is one EM transmission; another is policy space, with a Mexican central bank official telling Reuters that Fed hikes will limit Mexico's monetary policy [[n1923]].
Credit Check

Credit is softening, not breaking. HYG closed at 82.89 USD (+0.14% on 18 February, -2.98% over 20 sessions), LQD at 123.68 USD (-4.05%) and EMB at 103.00 USD (-2.45%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18); the investment-grade loss reflects duration more than spread. Reuters reported global companies slowing debt-raising as yields climb [[n1147]], and Barron's said Fidelity National Information Services pulled a capital-markets sale [[n0710]]. Artemis reported insurance bonds showing resilience as spreads reset [[n1141]]. Al Jazeera had described emerging markets dreading deja vu as Fed hikes loom [[n1888]], and Russia-linked issuers are the direct sanctions risk, with the Guardian listing London-listed Russian firms that could be hit [[n0748]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Leverage is coming out: Wolf Street reported margin debt plunging as stocks tumbled and high-fliers got crushed, though leverage remains gigantic [[n1165]]. ARKK fell -9.87% over five sessions to 64.80 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) as Bloomberg described Cathie Wood's innovation ETF as a year from its peak and still struggling [[n1557]], while CNBC quoted Wood calling her stocks 'way undervalued' [[n1579]]. Disclosed institutional buying is value-tilted: Yahoo Finance reported Warren Buffett investing $1B in Bitcoin-friendly Nubank [[n0373]] and Berkshire Hathaway buying $1 billion of Activision shares weeks before Microsoft's surprise acquisition [[n0374]]. Primary supply is lining up where demand is deep: Reuters reported Indian insurer LIC set to launch an $8 bln IPO on March 11 [[n1715]].
Portfolio Implication

Own liquidity and real assets, and rent duration tactically. Keep a modest long in the 10Y via IEF as a geopolitical hedge, but not at TLT size, because a half-point March move would extend front-end losses. Pair underweights in high-beta growth (ARKK, and TQQQ at 50.44 USD, -10.99% over 20 sessions) with overweights in energy and gold, and within credit prefer short-dated investment grade to high yield until HYG's -2.98% 20-session slide stabilises. Trigger: a further rise in the VIX from 27.75 index points on the US reopen would justify adding to the duration hedge. What changes the call: a VIX close back below its 20-session reference of 28.85 index points, with HYG stabilising, would signal that liquidity stress is passing and that beta can be rebuilt.

anticipatory.title: The Western sanctions response to the Donbas recognition
parts: What Is Priced

European equities priced a partial shock on 21 February, with the Euro Stoxx 50 -2.17% and the DAX -2.07% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21), but US cash equities last traded on 18 February, with the S&P 500 at 4,348.87 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Reuters had mapped how a Russia-Ukraine conflict might hit global markets [[n0759]].
Conditional Expression

If sanctions reach energy flows or Nord Stream 2, own XLE and gold against European autos; Putin's claim that Nord Stream 2 would cement Europe's energy security, reported by Reuters [[n1087]], shows how central the pipeline is to Moscow's leverage. If measures stay financial, fade the energy spike and buy quality European exporters.
Risk

Moscow has threatened retaliation, with Sky News quoting Lavrov saying Russia would retaliate if the UK imposed new sanctions [[n1221]], and The New Yorker argued the threat of more sanctions may not deter Putin [[n1197]]. A counter-sanction on commodity exports would hit European industry hardest.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: a quarter point or a half
parts: What Is Priced

Reuters' poll has a 25 bps March hike, with calls for 50 bps growing louder [[n1139]]. The 2Y at 1.47% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18), up +46 bps in 20 observations, already embeds an aggressive path, and Reuters compiled what global banks forecast for Fed rate hikes in 2022 [[n1928]].
Conditional Expression

If Fed speakers lean toward a quarter point, in line with the New York Fed president's 'no need for a big hike' message [[n1930]], the 2Y can retrace and growth can outperform financials. If the front-loaded campaign that James Bullard again called for, per the WSJ [[n1153]], wins out, flatteners and short-duration value outperform.
Risk

A geopolitical growth shock could tempt the Fed to do less, but Al Jazeera reported the Fed is prepared for faster hikes if inflation persists [[n1911]], and Barron's examined how stocks perform just before and after a drastic Fed increase [[n0713]]. Governance adds noise: Politico reported Republicans delaying the vote on Biden's Fed nominees [[n1904]], leaving the Board's composition unsettled into the decision.

anticipatory.title: Home Depot and Lowe's: housing's spending test
parts: What Is Priced

Home Depot closed at 346.87 USD (-0.64% over 20 sessions) and Lowe's at 222.69 USD (-1.04%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), a modest discount given Reuters' preview that cooling home-improvement demand may pressure their 2022 sales [[n1029]].
Conditional Expression

A strong sales guide would validate the housing wealth effect, as Reuters reported existing home sales accelerating [[n1879]], and favour Home Depot over discretionary peers such as Target, which is -5.92% over 20 sessions at 204.39 USD. A cautious guide would confirm that mortgage rates at a 33-month high [[n1867]] are biting, and would argue for selling Lowe's against Home Depot rather than buying either.
Risk

The Guam Daily Post reported new-home construction falling 4.1% [[n1880]], while The Real Economy Blog said housing permits reached a 15-year high [[n1858]]. Fortune reported Zillow expecting home prices to spike 22% this spring [[n0652]], which supports ticket sizes, but NPR said first-time buyers are being squeezed out by investors [[n1874]]. Mixed housing signals make guidance, not the quarter, the swing factor, and a miss would reinforce the Bearish discretionary call.

anticipatory.title: An Iran nuclear deal and the oil premium
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.07 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) carry a Russia premium, and XLE's +8.97% 20-session gain to 68.05 USD embeds it in equities. The State Department said Iran talks are in their 'very final stages', Reuters reported [[n1217]].
Conditional Expression

A deal would release barrels with a lag, because Reuters reported the draft puts prisoners, enrichment and cash first, with oil coming later [[n1230]]. Express it by trimming refiners and the most oil-levered producers, not by exiting energy, since the Russia premium would still dominate. Shuttle diplomacy continues, with Al Jazeera reporting Iran's Raisi discussing the talks with Qatar's emir in Doha [[n1288]].
Risk

Al Jazeera reported Iran's parliament setting conditions for a return to the deal [[n1272]], and the OPEC+ ministerial line was to keep maintaining balance in oil markets [[n0125]]. A failed deal leaves Saudi Arabia's rejection of Biden's plea for more production, reported by The Intercept [[n1644]], as the binding constraint.

catalysts.title: General Dynamics (GD) — US armour for a frontline ally
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported the US announced Abrams tanks for Poland as the Russia threat mounts [[n1375]], and DW said the US is set to sell them [[n1376]]. For US land-systems primes such as General Dynamics, an ally re-equipping on NATO's eastern flank converts geopolitical risk into backlog.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 215.82 USD, +0.66% on 18 February and +4.49% over 20 sessions, while ITA fell -0.84% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: defence budgets move slowly, and a diplomatic de-escalation would unwind the premium.
Trade Expression
Buy GD against ITA as a relative-value escalation hedge; add if the stock holds above 215.82 USD through the reopen, and cut if a Biden-Putin meeting is actually scheduled.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT) — the inflation share-taker
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The WSJ said Walmart withstood pandemic blows and higher costs to boost business [[n1008]], and Al Jazeera described it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0662]]. Grocery share gains [[n0661]] make it the defensive compounder in a stagflation scare.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Walmart closed at 137.99 USD, -0.64% on 18 February but +1.97% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: CNBC's report that shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0664]] could cap volumes, and Reuters said Walmart's Mexico unit saw profit rise 5% while costs increased [[n0976]], the margin tension in miniature.
Trade Expression
Own WMT against XLY; add on a hold above 137.99 USD on the reopen. What changes the call: fuel and freight costs squeezing margins faster than prices can be raised.

catalysts.title: Home Depot (HD) — guidance over the quarter
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Home Depot's pending report arrives as Reuters warns cooling home-improvement demand may pressure 2022 sales [[n1029]]. The thesis is that professional customers and pricing protect margins even as do-it-yourself volumes normalise, while RetailWire's report that Yeti is leaving Lowe's to focus on direct sales [[n1023]] hints that brands are choosing channels more selectively.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 346.87 USD, -0.31% on 18 February and -0.98% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: mortgage rates at their highest since May 2019 [[n1865]] slow housing turnover, the demand engine for renovation.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral into the print; buy on a guide that holds sales flat or higher with the stock above 346.87 USD, or sell Lowe's against it if guidance diverges.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA) — capacity bet versus multiple
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

NVIDIA's fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0084]] came with an upbeat revenue forecast [[n1661]], and TechSpot reported it spent $10 billion for a chunk of TSMC's 5nm capacity [[n1739]]: management is underwriting demand. The FTC said the termination of its Arm bid bodes well for competition [[n1674]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 236.42 USD, -3.53% on 18 February and -1.28% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: the 2Y's +46 bps 20-observation rise compresses long-duration multiples faster than estimates rise, and AMD at 113.83 USD competes for the same data-centre budgets.
Trade Expression

Accumulate on weakness only while SOXX holds its +0.55% five-session gain, and avoid the levered SOXL (-9.33% over 20 sessions). What changes the call: a close back above the 233.74 USD level of 21 January would show the guide being rewarded.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC) — the roadmap credibility discount
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Intel laid out an aggressive plan: PCWorld said its CPU roadmap spurs power efficiency [[n1703]], and CNET relayed Intel's claim that the chip technology for 2025 PCs is going great [[n1717]]. Fast Company's account of the $43.5B revival plan [[n0601]] signals heavy spending before returns, and the New York Times framed the question as whether Intel can make a comeback [[n0651]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Intel closed at 45.04 USD, -5.32% on 18 February and -13.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk to the Bearish call: the $5.4 billion Tower Semiconductor acquisition [[n0298]] could accelerate foundry revenue.
Trade Expression
Underweight INTC against AMD (113.83 USD); reconsider above the 52.04 USD level of 21 January, which would show the market crediting the roadmap.

catalysts.title: Digital World Acquisition (DWAC) — Truth Social's launch test
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Truth Social went live: Reuters reported it topped downloads on Apple's App Store with many users waitlisted [[n1610]], while Bloomberg said the app showed errors on launch day [[n1623]]. For DWAC, the SPAC for Trump Media & Technology Group, adoption is the valuation input.
Price Hurdle & Risk
